snapshots.name: Achilles
snapshots.body: The greatest warrior among the Greeks, son of the mortal Peleus and the sea-goddess Thetis. His quarrel with Agamemnon over a captive woman opens the poem and drives him to withdraw from the fighting.

snapshots.name: Hector
snapshots.body: Champion of Troy and eldest son of King Priam, husband of Andromache and father of the infant Astyanax. He leads the Trojan defense of the city against the invading Greek army.

snapshots.name: Agamemnon
snapshots.body: King of Mycenae and commander-in-chief of the assembled Greek forces, elder brother of Menelaus. His seizure of Achilles's captive Briseis touches off the quarrel that shapes the poem.

snapshots.name: Ulysses
snapshots.body: King of Ithaca, valued among the Greek leaders for his cunning and persuasive speech. He serves as a trusted counselor to Agamemnon and undertakes several of the war's more delicate missions.

snapshots.name: Patroclus
snapshots.body: Achilles's closest companion, son of Menoetius, raised alongside Achilles from boyhood. He remains at the ships with his friend after the quarrel with Agamemnon.

snapshots.name: Menelaus
snapshots.body: King of Sparta and younger brother of Agamemnon, whose wife Helen's departure with the Trojan prince Paris is the cause of the war. He fights among the foremost Greek chieftains.

snapshots.name: Ajax
snapshots.body: Towering son of Telamon, reckoned the strongest of the Greeks after Achilles. He commands the contingent from Salamis and repeatedly serves as the army's most reliable bulwark in defense.

snapshots.name: Diomed
snapshots.body: Young king of Argos, son of Tydeus, counted among the boldest of the Greek captains. He fights with a ferocity that at times draws him into combat even with the gods.

snapshots.name: Nestor
snapshots.body: Aged king of Pylos, the oldest and most experienced of the Greek chieftains. He offers counsel to Agamemnon and the other captains, often recalling the deeds of an earlier generation.

snapshots.name: Priam
snapshots.body: Aged king of Troy, father of Hector, Paris and many other sons and daughters. He rules the besieged city from its walls, watching the war press ever closer to its gates.

snapshots.name: Paris
snapshots.body: Trojan prince also called Alexandrus, whose abduction of Helen from Sparta is the war's original cause. Younger brother of Hector, he fights among the Trojans though less renowned as a warrior.

snapshots.name: Andromache
snapshots.body: Hector's wife and mother of their infant son Astyanax, daughter of a king whose city Achilles has already destroyed. She watches the war from within the walls of Troy.

snapshots.name: Helen
snapshots.body: Wife of Menelaus, whose departure with Paris to Troy is the cause of the war between the Greeks and the Trojans. She is renowned in both camps as the most beautiful woman of her age.

snapshots.name: Hecuba
snapshots.body: Queen of Troy, wife of Priam and mother of Hector, Paris and their many siblings. She watches over her family from within the city as the siege continues.

snapshots.name: Aeneas
snapshots.body: Trojan prince and kinsman of Priam's line, son of the mortal Anchises and the goddess of love. He commands troops among Troy's allies and fights among its foremost defenders.

snapshots.name: Sarpedon
snapshots.body: King of Lycia and son of the king of the gods, leader of the Trojans' most valued allied contingent. He crosses the sea to fight at Troy out of loyalty to Priam's cause.

snapshots.name: Phoenix
snapshots.body: Aged tutor and foster-father of Achilles, who reared him from childhood. He accompanies the Greek army at Troy and remains close to his former charge.

snapshots.name: Briseis
snapshots.body: Captive woman awarded to Achilles as a prize of war, taken from a captured town before the poem opens. Agamemnon's seizure of her from Achilles ignites the quarrel that opens the story.

snapshots.name: Chryseis
snapshots.body: Daughter of a priest of the god of prophecy and archery, held captive by Agamemnon. Her father's plea for her return, refused by Agamemnon, brings a plague upon the Greek camp.

snapshots.name: Thetis
snapshots.body: Sea-goddess and mother of Achilles by the mortal Peleus. She intercedes on her son's behalf with the king of the gods when he is wronged by Agamemnon.

snapshots.name: Jove
snapshots.body: King of the gods, whose will ultimately governs the course of the war despite the interventions of the other gods. He presides over Olympus from its highest peak.

snapshots.name: Juno
snapshots.body: Queen of the gods and wife of the king of the gods, an outspoken partisan of the Greek cause. She works, often deviously, to see Troy fall.

snapshots.name: Minerva
snapshots.body: Goddess of wisdom and warfare, born from the king of the gods, and among the Greeks' most active divine supporters. She intervenes directly in battle and in the counsels of mortals.

snapshots.name: Apollo
snapshots.body: God of the sun, prophecy and archery, and Troy's most committed divine protector. He sends the plague that opens the story's central quarrel and champions the Trojans throughout.

snapshots.name: Neptune
snapshots.body: God of the sea, who favors the Greek cause though bound by the king of the gods's decree not to intervene openly. He watches the war from the sea and occasionally acts in secret.

snapshots.name: Venus
snapshots.body: Goddess of love and mother of the Trojan prince Aeneas, a partisan of Troy. She protects Paris and involves herself in the affairs of the mortals she favors.

snapshots.name: Mars
snapshots.body: God of war, who fights on the Trojan side against the wishes of several of the other gods. His interventions in battle draw the anger of the war's Greek-aligned deities.

snapshots.name: Vulcan
snapshots.body: The gods' divine smith and craftsman, husband of the goddess of love. He forges arms and armor of great renown for favored mortals.

snapshots.name: Mercury
snapshots.body: Messenger of the gods, called on for tasks that require unseen or swift passage between Olympus and the mortal world.

snapshots.name: Ajax son of Oileus
snapshots.body: Swift-footed captain of the Locrians, son of Oileus, distinguished from the greater Ajax by his smaller stature and cunning. He fights alongside his more famous namesake.

snapshots.name: Idomeneus
snapshots.body: Veteran king of Crete, a trusted ally of Agamemnon. He leads the Cretan contingent and fights among the senior Greek chieftains.

snapshots.name: Glaucus
snapshots.body: Lycian captain and close companion of Sarpedon, son of Hippolochus. He fights beside Sarpedon among the Trojans' allies.
